In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HMTTeF complexes have very low resistivities, and that these low resistivities are caused by intermolecular interactions through the tellurium atoms in the complex molecules.
the electrical properties of HMTTe complexes depend strongly on the structure of the complex and the nature of the π-acceptor.
the tellurium atom is an excellent electron acceptor and a good donor, and the HMTTeF molecule has the potential to act as a good π-acceptor and a good π-donor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrical conductivity of the charge transfer complexes of π-donors and π-acceptors is controlled by the nature of the π-acceptor.
the electrical conductivity in the organic conductor is strongly affected by the molecular structure of π-acceptors.
the tellurafulvalene complexes show the lowest resistivity among the organic conductors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tellurium is not only an excellent π-electron acceptor but also a good π-donor.
the tellurium atoms in these complexes can be considered as a new kind of π-acceptor.
tellurium is a good element for constructing organic conductors, and that it is possible to obtain organic conductors with low activation energy and high conductivity.
